about.title: About Majlisna
about.name: Souhib TRABELSI
about.bio: Software engineer with more than 6 years of experience specializing in backend development with Python (FastAPI, Flask), React, and cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP). Experienced across the full software lifecycle — from frontend to deployment on cloud and on-premise infrastructures. Passionate about clean architecture, real-time apps, and building technology for the Islamic community.
about.lede: Majlisna (مجلسنا) means “our majlis”: the room where people sit together. It keeps the old samar alive, the evening of talk and riddles among friends.
about.games: The riddles are four party games you may already know, Undercover, Codenames, Kalimat and The Quiz, played in Islamic words: prophets, companions, places, practices, the Qur’an and the seerah. Every word comes with its explanation, so a round ends with something learned as well as a winner.
about.languages: English, French and Arabic are equals. At the same table, each player reads the hints and explanations in their own language, and the Arabic interface reads right to left from the first screen to the last.
about.creditsLine: The photographs, typefaces and icons Majlisna is made with are credited on the <page>Credits</page> page.
about.educationEpitech: Epitech Paris — Master’s in Software Engineering
about.experienceMaduraTitle: Madura Capital Management — Python Developer / DevOps
about.experienceMaduraDesc: Development of internal tools and automation systems to streamline trading operations and data flows within the hedge fund. Built data feeders, Prefect ETL pipelines, and a React TypeScript interface for trade management. Designed a clean FastAPI backend with CI/CD pipelines.
about.experienceSnapDesc: Development and deployment of a dashboard for Snaplab team members to record user sessions during tests of Snap’s Connected Spectacles. Built backend with FastAPI, deployed on AWS ECS with Terraform, and created a React TypeScript frontend on AWS Amplify.
about.experienceEnedisDesc: Development and deployment of a platform allowing users to follow up on their Enedis requests and exchange via chat. Built with FastAPI, deployed on AWS Lambda with Serverless framework, and React TypeScript frontend on AWS Amplify.
about.experienceBnpTitle: BNP Paribas Personal Finance — Python Developer / DevOps
about.experienceBnpDesc: Transitioned monolithic architecture to microservices. Created and deployed Python APIs enabling data scientists to run IDEs connected to a NAS for accessing large volumes of sensitive data inside protected infrastructures.
about.experienceCloudeasierDesc: Developed solutions enabling companies to reduce Cloud infrastructure costs. Built Python scripts on AWS Lambda and GCP Cloud Functions for compute instance pricing and scheduling, deployed via Terraform.
about.mentoringText: With my experience I can help CS engineers, developers, or anyone who wants to learn more about computer science — freely. I can also help with your resume, understanding the job market, preparing for interviews, or giving general advice when looking for jobs. Contact me via email or phone. If I don’t answer, leave a message and I’ll call you back.

rules.title: How the games play
rules.intro: The host opens a room, picks the game and shares the code. Here is what happens once everyone is seated.

undercover.step1: Each player receives an Islamic term in secret. Most share the same one; the undercover player holds a close but different one. In larger rooms one player may be Mr. White, who receives no word at all.
undercover.step2: In turn, everyone describes their word in a few words, without saying it.
undercover.step3: Then the table votes. The player with the most votes leaves the circle and their role is shown.
undercover.step4: A Mr. White who is voted out gets one guess at the shared word: a right guess wins the game for the impostors. Otherwise the civilians win once every impostor is out, and the impostors win as soon as they are as many as the civilians left.

codenames.step1: Two teams, each with a spymaster. The board holds twenty-five Islamic terms, and only the spymasters see which belong to which team.
codenames.step2: The spymaster gives a one-word clue and a number: how many cards it points to.
codenames.step3: The operatives choose cards one at a time, up to one more than the number. A card of your team lets you go on; a neutral card or one of the other team’s ends your turn.
codenames.step4: The first team to find all of its cards wins. Choose the assassin and your team loses at once.

wordQuiz.step1: A term is hidden behind six hints, from vague to precise. A new hint appears every few seconds.
wordQuiz.step2: Type your answer as soon as you know it. Arabic diacritics, capitals and extra spaces do not count against you.
wordQuiz.step3: The earlier you answer, the more it is worth: six points at the first hint, one at the last.
wordQuiz.step4: Each round ends with the answer explained. The highest score after the last round wins.

mcqQuiz.step1: Each question has four choices and one right answer, against the clock: fifteen seconds, unless the host sets another time.
mcqQuiz.step2: You get one attempt per question: your answer locks in when you choose it.
mcqQuiz.step3: A right answer is worth one point, and up to two more when it is fast.
mcqQuiz.step4: After each question, the explanation behind the answer is shown. The highest score at the end wins.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Majlisna (majlisna.app) is a free online platform for Islamic party games, run by Souhib Trabelsi. This page explains what data we collect, why, and how you can control it.

sections.title: Data we collect
body: Account: your username, email address and password (stored only as a hash). Optionally your country, a short bio and a profile picture.
Google sign-in: if you choose "Continue with Google", we receive your Google account identifier, email address, name and profile picture. We never receive your Google password.
Gameplay: rooms you join, games played, scores, statistics, achievements, challenges, friends and the chat messages you send in game rooms.
Technical data: server logs (such as IP address and browser type) for security and troubleshooting, and error reports when the app crashes.

sections.title: How we use it
body: To create and secure your account, run multiplayer games, show leaderboards and statistics, send account emails (verification and password reset) and keep the service working and safe. We do not sell your data and we do not show advertising.

sections.title: Service providers
body: Google (sign-in with Google and web fonts), Resend (sending account emails), Cloudflare (network and security proxy) and Oracle Cloud (server hosting). Audience statistics use a self-hosted Umami instance without advertising cookies; error reports go to a self-hosted error tracker.

sections.title: Retention
body: Your account data is kept until you delete your account. Server logs and error reports are kept for a limited period for security and debugging.

sections.title: Your rights
body: You can edit your profile at any time and delete your account from your profile page; deletion removes your account and the data linked to it. If you signed up with Google, or for any other request (access, correction, deletion, objection), contact us by email.

sections.title: Children
body: Majlisna is intended for a general audience. Children should use it with the permission of a parent or guardian.

sections.title: Changes
body: We may update this policy. The date at the top of this page shows the latest version.
